title: Adic line-system comparison through cofinal indices and rational coefficient colimits
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small relative to a larger sheaf universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with finite limits, and $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ a functor preserving finite limits and coverings. Let $L$ be its geometric inverse image [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]. Let $I$ be a nonempty directed poset whose underlying set belongs to the sheaf universe. For each $i\in I$ let $(R_{i,m})_{m\ge1}$ and $(S_{i,m})_{m\ge1}$ be inverse towers of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$. Write $R_i=\varprojlim_mR_{i,m}$ and $S_i=\varprojlim_mS_{i,m}$ [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Assume compatible ring isomorphisms $a_{i,m}:LR_{i,m}\cong S_{i,m}$ and a ring isomorphism $a_i:LR_i\cong S_i$ whose $m$-th projection is $a_{i,m}L(\mathrm{pr}_m)$.
Choose integers $e_i\ge1$ and put $B_{i,n}=R_{i,e_in}$, $B'_{i,n}=S_{i,e_in}$. Let $(M_{i,n})_n$ be a tower of $B_{i,n}$-module sheaves and $(N_{i,n})_n$ a tower of $B'_{i,n}$-module sheaves, with semilinear transitions [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume compatible isomorphisms $c_{i,n}:LM_{i,n}\cong N_{i,n}$ semilinear over $a_{i,e_in}$. For each $i$ assume one covering $\{V_{ij}\to1_{\mathcal C}\}_j$ and compatible bases $b_{ij,n}:B_{i,n}|_{V_{ij}}\cong M_{i,n}|_{V_{ij}}$, with $t_nb_{ij,n+1}=b_{ij,n}\rho_n$, on the localized sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Put $M_i=\varprojlim_nM_{i,n}$, $N_i=\varprojlim_nN_{i,n}$, with scalar actions via $R_i,S_i$ and their subsequence projections.
Assume also specified directed diagrams in $i$ of the pairs $(B_{i,n},M_{i,n})$ and $(B'_{i,n},N_{i,n})$ for every $n$, with ring homomorphisms and semilinear module maps commuting with the tower transitions, $a$ and $c$. Their induced limit diagrams are required to use the corresponding ring maps $R_i\to R_j$, $S_i\to S_j$. Let $s_i\in R_i(1_{\mathcal C})$ be compatible global sections, and let $s'_i=a_i(Ls_i)$. For a module $M$ over $R$ write $M[1/s]$ for the sheafified sequential colimit $M\xrightarrow{s}M\xrightarrow{s}\cdots$, with its canonical action of the likewise localized ring $R[1/s]$; equivalently this is $M\otimes_RR[1/s]$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then the projection equations
$$\mathrm{pr}_n\theta_i=c_{i,n}L(\mathrm{pr}_n)$$
define isomorphisms $\theta_i:LM_i\cong N_i$ semilinear over $a_i$, independent of the bases and natural in all the specified tower maps. They extend uniquely along the localization cocones to compatible isomorphisms
$$LM_i[1/s_i]\cong N_i[1/s'_i].$$
Here $LM_i[1/s_i]$ means $L(M_i[1/s_i])$. On the sheafified filtered colimits in $i$ they induce an isomorphism
$$L\bigl(\varinjlim_iM_i[1/s_i]\bigr)\cong\varinjlim_iN_i[1/s'_i],$$
semilinear over $L(\varinjlim_iR_i[1/s_i])\cong\varinjlim_iS_i[1/s'_i]$. The scalar action on each filtered colimit is the sheafification of $[r_i][m_j]=[r_km_k]$ at any common upper bound $k\ge i,j$. All comparisons are fixed by the displayed projections, localization maps and colimit coprojections. Restricting a compatible sequence to $m=e_in$ identifies the full coefficient limits with these subsequence limits; the inverse takes its $m$-th coordinate by reducing any coordinate at $e_in\ge m$.

source.place: The integral twist and Rational and algebraic closure paragraphs, abstracted to semilinear module systems. Stacks sites.tex Tag 03CF, lemma-localize-morphism, supports the localized tower argument; the expanded argument is preserved in report.md.

proof.text: For each positive stride, view $n\mapsto e_i(n+1)-1$ as a final monotone functor on $\mathbb N$; $n\le e_i(n+1)-1$ gives cofinality and thinness gives the parallel-arrow condition. Its opposite is initial. Whisker the given full ring limit cone and use uniqueness of limit points to obtain the prescribed cofinal isomorphism. Its forward equation is the limit factorization equation; cancel its isomorphism to derive the inverse-coordinate formula from cone naturality.

Apply the pointwise integral comparison lemma and choose its normalized linear isomorphism for every $i$. Set the coefficient lifts exactly equal to the supplied integral coefficient lifts. This already gives their required underlying-ring equality.

Construct the integral pair comparison. For $i\le j$, project its desired naturality square to any level $n$. The two limit-cone naturality equations and the supplied level-comparison square identify the projected maps. The additive limit, evaluated on every object and forgotten to sets, is a limit, so its projections are jointly monic. This proves naturality. The same sectionwise limit-extensionality argument shows that every set-sheaf map satisfying the displayed projections is the constructed comparison; it uses no linearity hypothesis on this competing map.

Apply the localization comparison to the constructed integral comparison, with the compatible sections and the given inverse-image section equations. This produces both localization pair diagrams, their natural normalized comparison, and the required uniqueness.

Apply the proved filtered-colimit existence theorem on both sites. This constructs the common-stage scalar actions and colimit pairs. Apply the filtered-colimit comparison to these supplied pairs and the localization comparison, obtaining the normalized algebraic inverse-image comparison.

The forgetful functors from additive and commutative-ring sheaves to set sheaves preserve filtered colimits. To see this with independent site universes, pass to a small model and transport the sheafification comparison back; present any sheaf diagram as the sheafification of its underlying presheaf diagram. Forgetful functors preserve filtered presheaf colimits, so the sheafification adjunction gives the desired preservation. The supplied adjunction makes $L$ preserve these colimits as well. Apply colimit hom-extensionality to the two source colimit cocones after forgetting and applying $L$. The coprojection equations of any two comparisons agree, so both their underlying ring and module maps, and hence their isomorphisms, agree.

proof_origin.place: Integral twist and Rational and algebraic closure paragraphs, with cofinality, naturality and both limit/colimit uniqueness arguments proved in Lean the common-stage filtered colimit constructed and three independent comparison results isolated.
